existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: R4 `MedicinalProduct` has a high-confidence R6 successor `MedicinalProductDefinition`, but the migration is hard-breaking. Top concerns are the resourceType/canonical rename, graph-level splits for package/pharmaceutical/authorization data, and same-name fields whose JSON type changed. The main uncertainty is exact official mapping for split resources because no official diff or ConceptMap was available locally.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should start with a root resource rename and reference retargeting, then apply local field transforms. Simple path rewrites handle some data (`productClassification` -> `classification`, `paediatricUseIndicator` -> `pediatricUseIndicator`, name substructure renames), but package, pharmaceutical, operation, and special-designation data often require creating related R6 resources. R6-to-R4 downgrade must preserve modifier `status` and R6-only content through extensions or sidecar mappings if round-trip fidelity matters.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for the presence, type, cardinality, binding, and flag differences because they come directly from local core StructureDefinitions and package indexes. Confidence is medium for some migration destinations because those are inferred from related R6 resource definitions rather than an official R4-to-R6 mapping or narrative migration guide.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
MedicinalProduct has a resource-identity break: R4 MedicinalProduct has no same-named R6 resource; successor is MedicinalProductDefinition. That makes a resource-level migration program unavoidable before element-level compatibility can solve much.

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 0, which creates weak stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 98/100, producing migration shape `removed-or-replaced-resource`, major migration `Yes`, and compatibility posture `migration-program-dominates`.

10 finding(s) identify a yes/partial less-breaking base-design alternative, so the aggregate should not be used to dismiss local avoidability review.

10 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Prioritize an explicit migration map, successor-resource guidance, endpoint/search transition guidance, and compatibility profiles or aliases where they are cheap. Do not rely on preserving individual old element names to solve the main break.
